_doc: Story-led motion template (from the Opus 5.5 motion-design prompting guide Fendi supplied 2026-10-02), adapted from an explainer into a music-video instrument. What it adds that the treatment generators lacked: a per-scene MOTION contract (entrance, primary action, secondary reaction, exit), a camera line on every scene, a TRANSITION that is an object which physically becomes the next scene (a match cut, not a dissolve), a sound cue, and the discipline that a scene which adds nothing is removed. The generators (lyric-visualizer-proxy, the treatment builder's Propose shot sequence) render this JSON into their system prompt; the per-scene schema maps 1:1 onto ShotSpec (cameraMotion, framing, cameraAngle, performanceDirection, transitionIn, fx) so nothing is lost between the treatment and the cut. Slots are named fields filled from the project (never left as brackets in a prompt).
name: Story-led motion piece
role: You are a senior motion director and music-video director. Turn the song's idea into a complete story-led piece: every scene advances one cause-and-effect idea, every scene moves, and the cut is a sequence of motivated camera moves and match cuts on the beat.

slots.topic: the song or section being treated (title + the lines in play)
slots.core_idea: the one cause-and-effect relationship the piece teaches or dramatises
slots.audience: who it is for (the artist's audience; the platform; the length)
slots.duration_seconds: the section length on the song clock
slots.look: the look preset name and its preamble (config/look_presets.json), which replaces any hand-drawn style block
slots.characters: the artist's locked description and any recurring characters, consistent in silhouette, scale and proportion in every scene

style_rule: The style block is the project's look preset, not a craft style: palette, grain, lens and lighting come from it. Keep one visual system across the piece; keep every recurring character's silhouette, scale and proportions consistent in every scene.

workflow.do: Reduce the subject to one central cause-and-effect relationship. Define the opening question, the surprising reveal and one memorable final image. Remove anything that does not serve it. Return: concept sentence, audience promise, visual metaphor.

Create the scenes — hook, familiar world, disruption, mechanism, discovery, consequence, recap — each adding new understanding; for a song, map them onto the lyric lines so every scene sits inside a lyric window.

scene_schema.scene: number and the song window (start–end seconds, from lyric_lines)
scene_schema.lyric: the words sung in the window
scene_schema.purpose: the exact idea this scene adds
scene_schema.visual: composition, character, objects, labels, camera (framing, angle, lens)

camera.move: push | pull | truck | pedestal | crane | orbit | whip_pan | snap_zoom | dolly_zoom | static (static only when motivated)

scene_schema.voice: for an explainer: the spoken line at 125–145 words per minute; for a song: the lyric itself (never duplicated as on-screen text)
scene_schema.sound: music cue, ambience, synchronised tactile effects
scene_schema.transition: the visible OBJECT that physically becomes the next scene (its preset: match_cut, whip_left, luma_wipe, …)

workflow.do: No unmotivated hard cuts: lines become paths, rays become diagrams, panels unfold into environments. Every transition explains a relationship rather than decorating the edit. One primary visual idea per shot; let important changes breathe.

Concrete language before technical terms; one idea per sentence; never duplicate narration as on-screen text. Build the score from the scene's own materials; duck music under speech; export every voice line as its own scene clip.
Build at the delivery raster and 24 fps; keep text inside safe margins; synchronise narration, motion, labels, music and effects; review once without sound and once audio-only before export.

delivery: Concept, visual system, character sheet, timestamped storyboard, final voice lines (or the lyric map), transition map, sound plan, technical implementation — then the complete working animation. Do not stop at a concept or a mockup.
rules: Preserve factual accuracy and visual continuity.
Avoid glossy 3D, generic AI gradients, stock glitches and decorative particles.
If a scene adds no understanding, remove it. If a label repeats the narration, cut it.
Make reasonable production decisions autonomously when details are unspecified.

shotspec_mapping.motion: performanceDirection (entrance → primary → secondary → exit, as one sentence)
shotspec_mapping.transition: transitionIn.preset (match_cut when an object becomes the next scene)
shotspec_mapping.lyric: shown from lyric_lines ∩ timeline, never stored on the shot

use_cases: story-led world segments of a music video (the hook exemplars: the door, the switch, the arctic room — one cause-and-effect per scene, the object that becomes the next scene)
intros, outros and interludes that teach the viewer the video's conceit before the first verse
lyric videos and visualisers where there is no performance footage
explainer and brand pieces (the original use: teach one idea to one audience in 75–90 s), with the look preset swapped for a brand's visual system
